SUPERVISOR DISPATCH — USER RULING: the workbench paint surface is AGNOSTIC. Marker: AGNOSTICPAINT-0606, ledger req_0013 (resolve on landing).

USER, verbatim: "it currently is treated like its isolated for characters is the problem. it needs to be treated as 'this is an agnostic painting surface, put whatever u want here' since the reality is this: any thing at all is all just the same thing at this level. from here we materialize something and it gets then put on the face of a building or a shirt, or anything."

THE RESTRUCTURE (this amends WORKBENCH.md's architecture — update the ledger doc as part of the landing):
1. ONE PAINT SURFACE in the workbench, subject-agnostic — the /cutout chrome you just correctly mounted (CutoutToolRail/Inspector/StatusBar/PaintSurface) becomes THE painting home, not a character-fenced lens. Its roster = every paintable target /cutout serves TODAY: figure parts (face/body), vehicle parts (the per-part livery from MODELPAINT), stored materials, recipes-as-underlay, blank canvases, saved paint documents. Parity reference = CutoutRoute's full target system (MODELS rail + MATERIALS + RECIPES + blank/new + library), not the character subset.
2. The per-source PAINT lens REMAINS as the doorway: from a character (or later vehicle/material) subject, the lens opens THE one surface with that subject preloaded — same surface, same state machinery, zero forked mounts. One painting experience everywhere, exactly like the user said: at this level everything is the same thing.
3. MATERIALIZE is the routing verb: the surface's save/extract actions route output to the consumer the subject implies (figure doc, VehicleDoc part, material catalog → assignable to building faces/tiles/parts) — all existing door paths from MODELPAINT/materialize; no new persistence, just the one surface fronting them.
4. Update WORKBENCH.md: §1/§3 reflect the agnostic paint surface (the "cutout = PAINT lens" row gains this ruling's text); §6 step 8 re-sequences — /cutout retirement now follows AGNOSTIC-PAINT PARITY (this work), not all-four-source parity. The user has ruled /cutout dies as soon as this surface passes their test, to kill split-brain updates.
5. Until the flip: /cutout is FROZEN — note it in CutoutRoute's CAPTURE (one line: frozen pending workbench parity, see WORKBENCH.md) so no lane lands features there; the supervisor rejects any /cutout-touching commit from now on.

Parity discipline as always: a line-referenced capability table from CutoutRoute.tsx's CURRENT state (it has grown since the last audit — re-derive, don't reuse) posted before the build; deferrals listed never dropped. §8 one-painter law absolute. Explicit paths, docs/_index contract, P4 tests (target-open round-trip per family, materialize routing per consumer), verify green, resolve req_0013. READY FOR USER TEST — the user opening a shirt, a car door, a material, and a blank canvas in ONE surface and materializing from it is the PASS. The /cutout deletion flip is its own commit after their pass.
